sections.value:
**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES**, round 2 (final under C34), at `8024824250b6caae856a09a18fca95039f173ce0`.

The delta adds **no daemon read, RPC, process launch, timer or periodic round**. Send preflight adds argument-only checks per candidate command, using shared role/address, duration/reply, forced-reason and attachment-path rules. Attachment-path resolution is lexical, not a file read. Accepted blocks still execute at most 20 commands; existing parsing/materialization and verb-specific costs remain as priced in [round 1](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/pull/212#issuecomment-6756060656).

**Round-1 fixes:** F001 tracks fences forward from the beginning in Rust and TS, so the four-line quoted example is neither executed nor hidden. F002 checks the send path's pure refusals before dispatch: the HTTP regression tries nine invalid sends after a valid FYI, observes zero held FYIs and zero messages, then positively demonstrates that its instrument sees a valid held FYI. The stricter non-FYI role-send `--force` reason requirement is documented. S212-N001 uses existing bounded caller-text rendering for echoed commands/reasons and a 120-scalar summary fence; OMP clips its no-result reason. No additional I/O is introduced by these fixes.

**P212-N001 improved, residual C34 follow-up:** ordinary replies no longer split/allocate full line arrays per draw. Precisely, the production `render()` path calls `includes()` **twice** when no opener exists, not once; streaming also examines only the final 24 characters. Substring searches remain length-dependent, not constant work.

Replies containing an opener reuse their result while resident in separate 32-entry streaming and settled FIFO maps. Thus repeated resident redraws avoid the fence scan, but "once per distinct text" is conditional on residence. Changed streaming prefixes or evicted texts are scanned again; a working set above 32 can churn. The maps retain up to **64 whole-text keys plus rendered results per display**, bounded in entries, not bytes. Streaming scan/allocation work can still grow quadratically across fixed-size increments. These are source-priced tradeoffs and the remaining long-reply proof gap, not an established normal-use cost breach. No local benchmark is claimed.

The one logical candidate RPC, possible auth-refresh retry, 25-second deadline, bounded 50ms x40 idle-wait chain, existing verb launches and explicit setup recipe costs are unchanged. No new daemon launch site; all six spawn guards execute successfully.

**Exact-head CI:** [42738518665](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42738518665), successful Rust job `129573568657`, upload artifact **13727009911**, metadata pinned to this head: **2,366 executed passed**, zero failures/errors; six skips reported separately by nextest. JUnit names all 11 core turn-end cases and seven HTTP cases, including the new regressions. Node22 executes 15 core decision/render tests and six adapter tests; npm reports **2,281 passed, six skipped**. Node24, Rust lint and delivers also succeed. Worktree clean; GitHub head matches and is CLEAN.

No local build/test, mutation, synthetic traffic or new live sampling. The existing feature-off baseline remains in round 1. **After-deploy reading remains owed after merge/deployment**; this verdict does not clear other roles or lane B.
